# nanobot 🐈 **nanobot** is an ultra-lightweight, open-source, self-hosted personal AI agent framework written in Python. Use it in a browser, terminal, or chat app to work with files, remember preferences, and schedule tasks. Connect a supported model provider or local model server to supply the AI. ## Start Here | You want to... | Go to | |---|---| | Install nanobot with no terminal/config background | [Start Without Technical Background](./docs/start-without-technical-background.md) | | Install quickly and get your first reply | [Install](#-install) and [Quick Start](#-quick-start) | | Open the bundled browser UI | [WebUI](#-webui) | | Connect Telegram, Discord, WeChat, Slack, Email, Mattermost, Linear, or another channel | [Chat app guide](./docs/guides/chat-app-ai-agent.md) | | Configure providers, fallback models, Langfuse, MCP, web tools, or security | [Docs](./docs/README.md) and [Configuration](./docs/configuration.md) | | Develop the browser UI | [Install current source](#-install), then [WebUI development](./webui/README.md) and [Contributing](./CONTRIBUTING.md) | | Integrate from Python or HTTP | [Python SDK](./docs/python-sdk.md) or [Agent API](./docs/openai-api.md) | | Understand or extend the internals | [Architecture](./docs/architecture.md), [Contributing](./CONTRIBUTING.md), and [Provider extensions](./docs/development.md) | | Deploy to the cloud or keep nanobot running as a service | [Deployment](./docs/deployment.md) | ## What can nanobot do? nanobot can: - run in a browser WebUI or terminal - connect to Telegram, Discord, Slack, WeChat, Email, Mattermost, Linear, and other channels - read PDF, Word (`.docx`), Excel (`.xlsx`), and PowerPoint (`.pptx`) files with built-in file tools, for tasks such as summarizing reports - use shell, web search/fetch, MCP integrations, cron, image generation, and multi-agent delegation - keep session history and long-term memory through [Dream](./docs/memory.md#save-and-check-a-preference) - run [long-horizon goals](./docs/guides/long-running-ai-agent.md) and [scheduled automations](./docs/automations.md) - expose a Python SDK and OpenAI-compatible API for integrations - deploy as a long-running local or server-side agent gateway ## 💡 Why nanobot - **Persistent workflows**: keep saved conversations, long-term memory, and task results for later work. - **Chat-native reach**: WebUI, API, Telegram, Feishu, Slack, Discord, Teams, email, Mattermost, and Linear. - **Model freedom**: OpenAI-compatible APIs, local LLMs, image generation, search, and fallbacks. - **Small core**: readable internals with MCP, memory, deployment, and automation built in. - **Own your stack**: inspect, customize, self-host, and extend without a giant platform. ## 📦 Install You need **Python 3.11 or newer** and access to a [supported model provider or local model server](./docs/providers.md). Model fees or local hardware requirements depend on the service you choose; nanobot does not supply a model account. Choose the **stable release** for everyday use or **current source** for development and the latest features. This README describes current source; [published documentation](https://nanobot.wiki/docs/latest/getting-started/nanobot-overview) covers the released version. New to terminals or model credentials? Follow [Start Without Technical Background](./docs/start-without-technical-background.md). Updating an existing instance? Stop every old nanobot process using that workspace, back up its config directory and workspace, then update and restart through the original launcher or service. See [session storage and version changes](./docs/cli-reference.md#session-storage). **Stable release: automatic setup (recommended)** The installer chooses an isolated Python environment and opens setup for you. The two commands below are the same installation method for different operating systems; run only the one for your system.
macOS / Linux ```bash curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/HKUDS/nanobot/main/scripts/install.sh | sh ```
Windows PowerShell ```powershell irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/HKUDS/nanobot/main/scripts/install.ps1 | iex ```
Installer details, preview, and script review The installer installs or upgrades `nanobot-ai` using an active virtual environment, `uv`, `pipx`, or a managed venv under `~/.nanobot/venv`. Fresh local desktops open the WebUI; SSH, headless, existing-config, and older-release paths use the terminal setup wizard. Keep the printed command: it identifies the environment that owns the installation. To preview the plan without changing your environment, pass `--dry-run`. ```bash curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/HKUDS/nanobot/main/scripts/install.sh | sh -s -- --dry-run ``` ```powershell & ([scriptblock]::Create((irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/HKUDS/nanobot/main/scripts/install.ps1))) --dry-run ``` If you prefer to inspect the script first, open [`scripts/install.sh`](./scripts/install.sh) or [`scripts/install.ps1`](./scripts/install.ps1).
Already use uv or pip? Install the stable package yourself Use this instead of the recommended installer when you already manage your own Python environment. These commands install the same stable `nanobot-ai` package; they do not launch setup. **uv: isolated CLI installation** ```bash uv tool install nanobot-ai ``` **pip: activate your virtual environment first** ```bash python -m pip install nanobot-ai ``` Then run `nanobot webui` for browser setup, or `nanobot onboard --wizard` for terminal-only setup. For the [Python SDK](./docs/python-sdk.md), install `nanobot-ai` in your application's virtual environment so the application can import it; a separate `uv tool` environment does not make the SDK importable there. If pip reports `externally-managed-environment`, use the recommended installer, `uv tool install nanobot-ai`, `pipx install nanobot-ai`, or an activated virtual environment. Upgrade with the same method; for uv use `uv tool upgrade nanobot-ai`, and for pip use `python -m pip install -U nanobot-ai`.
**Current source: development checkout**
Install current source with Git and Bun Clone the repository and install it in editable mode. A source install requires Git and [Bun](https://bun.sh/); Bun runs the matching TUI directly from the checkout instead of downloading an older release binary. ```bash git clone https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot.git cd nanobot python -m venv .venv ``` Activate it with `source .venv/bin/activate` on macOS/Linux or `.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1` in Windows PowerShell, then run: ```bash python -m pip install -e . ``` After that, the normal commands are identical to a stable install. `nanobot` runs the TUI from this checkout, and `nanobot webui` rebuilds stale frontend assets automatically. After stopping the old instance, `git pull --ff-only` updates the Python, TUI, and WebUI source together; rerun `python -m pip install -e .` when Python dependencies change, then restart the instance. Contributors should also read [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](./CONTRIBUTING.md).

A source-distribution install can fetch a checksummed, version-matched TUI archive—with its licenses, notices, corresponding application source, source offer, and relinking instructions—on first use. Pip selects the matching wheel; opening the TUI does not need a separate GitHub download or Bun installation. A source-distribution install on a supported target can use the matching checksummed GitHub release archive. On other platforms, use `nanobot --classic` or the WebUI. > [!IMPORTANT] > > If you want the newest features and experiments, install from source. > > If you want the most stable day-to-day experience, install from PyPI or with `uv`. releases.name: v0.3.5
releases.body:
🐈 **nanobot `v0.3.5`** brings the workbench to the terminal — and makes conversations easier to continue across the browser, terminal, and chat apps.

The headline is **one agent, more places to work**. Run `nanobot` for the native terminal client or `nanobot webui` for the browser. Both use the same gateway and saved WebSocket conversations. Terminal sessions can be resumed, forked, inspected, and detached without building a separate agent runtime.

The browser workbench has grown around real multitasking: grouped conversation panes, temporary chats, persistent sidebar ordering, session mentions, a skills marketplace, portable Agent Plugins, and browser OAuth for remote MCP servers. Automations now have task and calendar views, clearer scheduling controls, and per-run replies. Mobile composition, settings, context charts, app logos, and branded mentions received another round of focused polish.

The other story is **continuity you can inspect**. Context usage and compaction are visible, interrupted work has clearer recovery controls, and session history is more durable across pagination, reconnects, and upgrades. This release also tightens attachment, process, workspace, and emai

releases.name: v0.3.0
releases.body:
🐈 **nanobot `v0.3.0`** is here: **260 PRs merged and 38 new contributors**. The agent gained agency.

The fastest way to experience the release is one command:

```bash
nanobot webui
```

It prepares the local WebUI, starts the gateway, and opens the browser workbench. On a fresh install, guided setup helps you choose a provider and configure access without beginning in a JSON file. The published package already includes the WebUI, so there is no separate frontend build.

The product story is **a WebUI that now feels like the front door to nanobot**. Chats read as topics; documents, quoted follow-ups, multimodal tool results, file diffs, code previews, and model fallback are visible in the conversation. Model presets can be switched from the composer, native desktop hosts can open a system folder picker, settings work better across narrow screens and dark mode, and the interface now includes Brazilian Portuguese plus substantially improved Traditional Chinese.

releases.name: v0.2.2
releases.body:
🐈 **nanobot `v0.2.2`** is here — 140 PRs merged, 21 new contributors. The agent got sturdier!

The headline is **durability**. WebUI conversations now survive more of real life: transcripts are segmented instead of living in one fragile file, forked chats preserve replies more reliably, active turns scroll and replay more predictably, startup paths block less, and gateway shutdown is much calmer. Long sessions, stale providers, slow routes, broken config files, malformed history, stream stalls, and empty provider responses all got less likely to derail the work.

The second story is **nanobot becoming a real Python runtime**. The SDK is no longer just a thin convenience layer around the agent loop: concurrent `run()` calls are isolated, hooks are cleaner, MCP lifecycle handling is safer, runtime controls are broader, and the docs now teach the SDK from first principles. If you want to embed nanobot inside your own application, `v0.2.2` is the first release where that path feels intentional.

releases.name: v0.2.1
releases.body:
🐈 **nanobot `v0.2.1`** is here — 84 PRs merged, 17 new contributors. The agent got a real workbench.

The headline is the **WebUI becoming the place where work actually happens**. The chat surface is smoother, faster, and easier to trust: live file edits show up as activity, tool traces render more cleanly, source links get readable favicons, markdown and code blocks behave better, new chats survive refreshes, and Thought / response ordering now matches the model's real turn structure. Settings, sidebar controls, model switching, context-window control, slash commands, project workspaces, and access modes all moved closer to a single coherent control surface.

The second story is **long-running work getting more durable**. Sustained goals no longer trip the runner, goal iteration budget is higher, session locks prevent overlapping turns from stepping on each other, AutoCompact and consolidation races were fixed, heartbeat moved onto cron, and session archive retention got several data-loss fixes. In practice, this means fewer mysterious interruptions, fewer duplicate archives, and a much better chance that a long agent workflow keeps its thread of intent.

releases.name: v0.2.0
releases.body:
🐈 **nanobot `v0.2.0`** is here 🎉 — 105 PRs merged, 20 new contributors. The agent learned to hold a goal.

The headline is `/goal`. Mark a thread as a sustained objective with `long_task`, and the active goal stays pinned in Runtime Context every turn — surviving compaction, surviving long tool chains, surviving the model's own forgetfulness — until you call `complete_goal`. The wall-clock timeout widens automatically while a goal is active; streaming requests fall back to an idle timeout instead of a hard wall, so a model that's still thinking doesn't get killed mid-thought.

The second story is the **WebUI growing up**. After several releases as a source-only preview, it now ships **inside the wheel** — `pip install nanobot-ai` and you have it. Settings and BYOK got a full redesign, the slash palette is localized, LAN access is gated by a token, reasoning streams live to the chat, and a brand-new image-generation tool turns "draw me X" into an inline preview without leaving the conversation.

The third story is **the engine room**. The agent loop got a real refactor — `AgentLoop.from_config()` for clean embedding, `_process_message` rewritten as a functional state machine

🐈 nanobot is an ultra-lightweight, open-source, self-hosted personal AI agent framework written in Python. Use it in a browser, terminal, or chat app to work with files, remember preferences, and schedule tasks. Connect a supported model provider or local model server to supply the AI.

What can nanobot do?

nanobot can:

  • run in a browser WebUI or terminal
  • connect to Telegram, Discord, Slack, WeChat, Email, Mattermost, Linear, and other channels
  • read PDF, Word (.docx), Excel (.xlsx), and PowerPoint (.pptx) files with built-in file tools, for tasks such as summarizing reports
  • use shell, web search/fetch, MCP integrations, cron, image generation, and multi-agent delegation
  • keep session history and long-term memory through Dream
  • run long-horizon goals and scheduled automations
  • expose a Python SDK and OpenAI-compatible API for integrations
  • deploy as a long-running local or server-side agent gateway

💡 Why nanobot

  • Persistent workflows: keep saved conversations, long-term memory, and task results for later work.
  • Chat-native reach: WebUI, API, Telegram, Feishu, Slack, Discord, Teams, email, Mattermost, and Linear.
  • Model freedom: OpenAI-compatible APIs, local LLMs, image generation, search, and fallbacks.
  • Small core: readable internals with MCP, memory, deployment, and automation built in.
  • Own your stack: inspect, customize, self-host, and extend without a giant platform.

📦 Install

You need Python 3.11 or newer and access to a supported model provider or local model server. Model fees or local hardware requirements depend on the service you choose; nanobot does not supply a model account.

Choose the stable release for everyday use or current source for development and the latest features. This README describes current source; published documentation covers the released version.

New to terminals or model credentials? Follow Start Without Technical Background. Updating an existing instance? Stop every old nanobot process using that workspace, back up its config directory and workspace, then update and restart through the original launcher or service. See session storage and version changes.

Stable release: automatic setup (recommended)

The installer chooses an isolated Python environment and opens setup for you. The two commands below are the same installation method for different operating systems; run only the one for your system.

macOS / Linux 
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/HKUDS/nanobot/main/scripts/install.sh | sh
Windows PowerShell 
irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/HKUDS/nanobot/main/scripts/install.ps1 | iex
Installer details, preview, and script review

The installer installs or upgrades nanobot-ai using an active virtual environment, uv, pipx, or a managed venv under ~/.nanobot/venv. Fresh local desktops open the WebUI; SSH, headless, existing-config, and older-release paths use the terminal setup wizard. Keep the printed command: it identifies the environment that owns the installation.

To preview the plan without changing your environment, pass --dry-run.

curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/HKUDS/nanobot/main/scripts/install.sh | sh -s -- --dry-run
& ([scriptblock]::Create((irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/HKUDS/nanobot/main/scripts/install.ps1))) --dry-run

If you prefer to inspect the script first, open scripts/install.sh or scripts/install.ps1.

Already use uv or pip? Install the stable package yourself

Use this instead of the recommended installer when you already manage your own Python environment. These commands install the same stable nanobot-ai package; they do not launch setup.

uv: isolated CLI installation

uv tool install nanobot-ai

pip: activate your virtual environment first

python -m pip install nanobot-ai

Then run nanobot webui for browser setup, or nanobot onboard --wizard for terminal-only setup. For the Python SDK, install nanobot-ai in your application's virtual environment so the application can import it; a separate uv tool environment does not make the SDK importable there.

If pip reports externally-managed-environment, use the recommended installer, uv tool install nanobot-ai, pipx install nanobot-ai, or an activated virtual environment. Upgrade with the same method; for uv use uv tool upgrade nanobot-ai, and for pip use python -m pip install -U nanobot-ai.

Current source: development checkout

Install current source with Git and Bun

Clone the repository and install it in editable mode. A source install requires Git and Bun; Bun runs the matching TUI directly from the checkout instead of downloading an older release binary.

git clone https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot.git
cd nanobot
python -m venv .venv

Activate it with source .venv/bin/activate on macOS/Linux or .venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1 in Windows PowerShell, then run:

python -m pip install -e .

After that, the normal commands are identical to a stable install. nanobot runs the TUI from this checkout, and nanobot webui rebuilds stale frontend assets automatically. After stopping the old instance, git pull --ff-only updates the Python, TUI, and WebUI source together; rerun python -m pip install -e . when Python dependencies change, then restart the instance. Contributors should also read CONTRIBUTING.md.

Supported platforms, bundled UIs, and release tracks

Published packages include the WebUI, and supported platform wheels also include the native TUI. A source-distribution install can fetch a checksummed, version-matched TUI archive—with its licenses, notices, corresponding application source, source offer, and relinking instructions—on first use.

Platform wheels include both the WebUI and the native terminal UI: macOS 13+ (Apple Silicon and Intel), glibc 2.17+ Linux (ARM64 and x64), and Windows x64. The x64 runtime requires SSE4.2. Pip selects the matching wheel; opening the TUI does not need a separate GitHub download or Bun installation. A source-distribution install on a supported target can use the matching checksummed GitHub release archive. On other platforms, use nanobot --classic or the WebUI.

[!IMPORTANT]

If you want the newest features and experiments, install from source.

If you want the most stable day-to-day experience, install from PyPI or with uv.

Pick one install method:

Track Install with Update with What runs
Stable installer, uv, or pip same installation method one released Python/WebUI/TUI version
Current source editable Git checkout git pull --ff-only + editable dependency sync Python, WebUI, and TUI from that checkout
Verify the installation or locate the nanobot command

Verify the install:

nanobot --version

If nanobot is not on PATH, invoke it through the method that installed it: reuse the recommended installer's command, use uv tool run --from nanobot-ai nanobot ... or pipx run --spec nanobot-ai nanobot ..., or use the Python executable from the environment where pip installed the package.

After installation, continue with Quick Start. Use the exact command printed by the installer if nanobot is not on PATH.

🚀 Quick Start

Open nanobot in your browser

If the installer already opened the WebUI, continue there. Otherwise run:

nanobot webui

Keep the launcher terminal open while using the browser. It starts or joins the shared local gateway and binds the first-run WebUI to localhost. If the browser does not open, copy the complete login link printed in the terminal, including everything after #; keep this credential private. For SSH or a headless host, use the remote-browser or terminal-only instructions below.

Your first three steps

  1. Open Settings → Models and save a provider/model preset with your credential or supported sign-in. See model setup if you need the full steps.
  2. Start a new topic and send Hello! to verify the model connection.
  3. To try file work, put a copy of notes.txt in a practice folder, select that folder and Restricted access, and ask: "Read notes.txt and write a short summary to summary.md." Open summary.md in that folder to check the result. See Your first file task.

A normal reply verifies the provider/model and browser connection. The file task separately checks the selected project and its file permissions. Attaching a file sends it to the conversation; it does not change the selected project folder.

Then describe your next goal in the same chat, for example: "I am already using the WebUI. Help me connect Telegram and allow only my account." An enabled nanobot-document skill can consult the documentation bundled with your installation; see Continue with nanobot for examples, explicit invocation, and availability.

Open the WebUI on a remote server through SSH

After installing nanobot on the server, start its WebUI without opening a server-side browser:

nanobot webui --no-open

Keep that server terminal running. In a second terminal on your own computer, forward the default WebUI port through SSH:

ssh -N -L 127.0.0.1:8765:127.0.0.1:8765 user@SERVER

Replace user@SERVER with your SSH login and leave the tunnel open. In your local browser, open the complete login link printed by the server launcher, preserving its # fragment. It uses http://127.0.0.1:8765, which now reaches the server through the tunnel. Complete Settings → Models and send Hello!. If local port 8765 is occupied, use another local port in the tunnel and change only the port in the browser link. Keep the server listener on localhost. For Docker, public endpoints, or service management, see Deployment.

Terminal-only setup, one-shot checks, and the TUI

If a model is not configured yet, use the terminal wizard:

nanobot onboard --wizard

Check one reply without opening the browser:

nanobot -m "Hello!"

For interactive work, open the terminal client:

nanobot

The native TUI uses the launch directory as its project workspace and shares saved conversations and the local gateway with the WebUI. The explicit nanobot agent form remains available for compatibility.

  • Type / to discover commands, /sessions to switch conversations, or @ to mention an app, MCP server, or saved session.
  • Paste clipboard images with Ctrl+V or Alt+V, and use $ to complete skill references.
  • Use /diff to inspect file changes, /context to inspect session context, or /branch to continue from a completed reply in a new session.
  • Press Enter to send. While nanobot is working, Enter sends now and Tab sends after the current response. Press Shift+Enter to add a newline (Ctrl+J works in terminals that cannot distinguish modified Enter keys).
  • Use /detach to promote the gateway to background mode and close the TUI while work continues.

Each launch starts a new session by default. Use --session to resume one and --workspace to choose another project workspace. See the CLI reference for session branching, diffs, history, shortcuts, gateway lifecycle, and compatibility options.

Save and check a preference

State a specific preference in your chat, for example: "For release notes, use concise bullet points." To consolidate it now, send /compact and then /dream, waiting for each to finish, and review /dream-log. Check the actual changes to USER.md or memory/MEMORY.md in the configured agent workspace, then test reuse in a new topic in the same instance. Dream may decide that no durable change is needed; a conversational acknowledgement alone does not prove the preference was saved. See Save and Check a Preference for file access, correction, and restoration steps.

Start and stop a sustained goal

Use a regular topic for a bounded objective with a clear completion condition, for example:

/goal Review this project's tests and list the smallest missing test case.

The goal lets nanobot continue work across model turns while the gateway runs; a scheduled automation instead starts a turn at specified times. Use /stop to interrupt the current work, and ask nanobot to cancel the goal if you want to abandon it. Keep the gateway running for unattended work using the background or service options below.

After a gateway restart, reopen the original topic and review saved results before explicitly continuing any interrupted work. Recovery does not blindly replay uncertain tool actions. See the long-running agent guide for starting conditions and related automation options.

Keep the gateway running after closing interactive clients

After model setup, keep channels and automations running when interactive launchers close:

nanobot gateway --background

This starts or promotes the shared gateway to a detached process. From the TUI, /detach does the same before closing that client. Background mode does not configure startup after a machine reboot or restart after a crash; use an OS-managed service for that. Interrupted subagent tasks are not automatically relaunched after a restart, and missed scheduled times are not replayed; see subagent recovery and automation delivery.

Manage the background gateway with:

nanobot gateway status
nanobot gateway logs
nanobot gateway restart
nanobot gateway stop

To reopen the browser, run nanobot webui against the same instance and use its complete printed login link.

Run a configured gateway directly

Use this once a model is configured and you want to run the gateway directly in the current terminal:

nanobot gateway

It skips guided WebUI setup and browser opening. The WebUI remains available when its channel is configured. Use nanobot gateway --background for a detached process, or follow Deployment for startup and supervision by the operating system.

Read task guides or look up configuration details
  • Model/provider recipes: Provider Cookbook and Providers and Models.
  • Local models: Ollama, vLLM or another OpenAI-compatible server.
  • Chat platforms: Chat app guide, then the full channel reference.
  • Exact settings for web search, MCP, voice, image generation, and security: Configuration.
  • Manual JSON and other setup paths: Install and Quick Start.
  • Failures after setup: Troubleshooting.

If nanobot worked for you, a star on GitHub is the simplest way to support the project.

☁️ Deploy

Render — one click

Deploy nanobot's gateway and bundled WebUI from the repository's ready-to-use Blueprint:

Render will ask for ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and a private NANOBOT_WEB_TOKEN, then provision persistent storage for sessions, memory, and WebUI history. Persistent disks require a paid Render service.

Self-host

Prefer your own infrastructure? Follow the deployment guide for Docker, Docker Compose, Linux services, and macOS LaunchAgent setup.

🌐 WebUI

The WebUI ships inside the published wheel with no separate frontend build. It is the browser workbench for persistent topics, temporary chats, visible agent activity, workspace controls, Apps, Skills, Automations, and settings. Start it with nanobot webui. WebUI access grants administration of the same agent instance; share it only with trusted operators. See Sharing access.

The screenshots below use example conversations, illustrative token counts, and paused schedules.

Use it to:

  • keep separate topics for different tasks and projects;
  • use temporary chats when a conversation should not be saved to history or memory;
  • inspect reasoning, tool calls, file edits, diffs, command output, and generated artifacts;
  • switch models and workspaces without leaving the conversation;
  • configure models in Settings, connect chat platforms in Channels, and manage Apps, Skills, and Automations.

Keep related work side by side

Group up to four conversations and arrange them in columns, rows, a grid, or a main pane with supporting panes. Each topic keeps its own history. Select another topic from the @ menu, or drag it into the composer, to let the agent read its context and coordinate work across sessions.

Choose a project, access mode, and model for each task. Topics separate conversation history; project folders select where file work happens. Neither creates separate long-term memory: one instance shares its agent profile, memory, and skills across projects. Use separate instances when client data or preferences must stay isolated. Explore topics and panes →

Inspect the work and its context

Expand agent activity to see reasoning, tool calls, and file changes. Switch Settings → Appearance → File edit display to Diff for inline patches. The composer's context indicator shows the current context size, input tokens by round, and cache reuse when the provider reports it.

Context compaction also appears in the conversation timeline. Explore activity and context →

Bring your tools into the conversation

Use Apps to connect MCP servers, enable Agent Plugins, and manage local CLI App adapters. Add a preset or a custom server, then attach an available tool with @. Skills provide reusable instructions. Settings holds model, voice, image, and web setup; Channels handles chat-platform connections.

Explore Apps → · Discover Skills → · Connect chat apps →

Before connecting a personal bot to shared channels, check the platform's DM pairing/allowlist and group-access policies separately. Approving a private sender does not restrict group access on every platform; see the channel reference.

Let recurring work run on a schedule

Ask for an automation from the topic that should receive its results. Use Tasks to review and manage schedules, or Calendar to scan completed and upcoming runs by date. Local triggers let a script start a saved task on demand.

Keep the gateway running and the host awake for scheduled delivery. Missed scheduled times are not replayed after a gateway restart. See delivery and recovery rules. Explore Automations →

For a conversation that should stay out of saved topic history and long-term memory, use Temporary chat from the header. Temporary chats end when the connection closes and use the default workspace in Restricted mode. Requests still go to the configured model provider, and files created by tools remain after the chat closes.

See the WebUI guide for LAN access, background operation, workspace controls, and the full feature tour. Working on the frontend itself? Use webui/README.md.

Architecture

The Python gateway owns agent execution, sessions, tools, memory, and security policy for the WebUI, TUI, and chat apps. The clients share that runtime; the core agent loop builds context, calls the model, executes requested tools, and returns the result. Memory, skills, channels, and MCP integrations extend that loop.

The Python SDK embeds the agent runtime in your application process. The OpenAI-compatible API starts a separate HTTP service for /v1/chat/completions: each request contains one user message, history is managed by the server, and the model comes from configuration. Responses return to the HTTP client; that service does not deliver tool messages to chat apps.

See Architecture for source ownership and extension points.

aiSummary.oneLiner: An ultra-lightweight, self-hosted Python framework for running persistent personal AI agents with native MCP support.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: Nanobot provides a minimalist framework for building and running personal AI agents locally or on a private server. It features a built-in WebUI and terminal interface, allowing users to interact with their agents seamlessly. The framework deeply integrates the Model Context Protocol (MCP), enabling agents to securely access local files, shell environments, and web tools. It maintains persistent long-term memory and session history, ensuring context survives between interactions. With its OpenAI-compatible API and broad chat app integrations, it serves as a versatile, private alternative to commercial agent platforms.
keyFeatures: Ultra-lightweight core: Designed for fast, efficient execution on local hardware without the bloat of large commercial agent frameworks.
Native MCP integration: Connects securely to Model Context Protocol servers to access databases, APIs, and local files.
Persistent memory system: Utilizes long-term memory storage to ensure agents remember context and goals across multiple sessions.
Broad chat integrations: Connects seamlessly to Telegram, Discord, Slack, and WeChat for ubiquitous access to your personal agent.
OpenAI-compatible API: Exposes a standard API endpoint, allowing the agent to function as a drop-in replacement in existing AI pipelines.
Scheduled automations: Supports cron-based triggers for running long-horizon goals and automated tasks in the background.
